A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pose Prior Learner work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original PPL evaluations on Human3.6m, Taichi, and CUB-200-2011, together with prior ablations, occlusion experiments, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds loss and memory ablations, computational measurements, and qualitative comparisons and failure analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed PPL retains the same affine keypoint transformations, connectivity prior, hierarchical memory retrieval and distillation, four losses, gradient handling, and iterative inference. The single-bank and sigmoid alternatives are new ablation controls, not revisions to the default method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same quantitative datasets and CUB subsets, use the same six qualitative object categories, and investigate random and central occlusion. The additional examples remain within this coverage. v3's discussion of excluding DeepFashion, CelebA, and Zebra does not remove datasets evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: v3 adds BKind to the Human3.6m comparison in Table 1 and Hedlin et al. (2024), using pretrained diffusion models, across Human3.6m, Taichi, and the CUB subsets in Table A2. It also introduces direct qualitative AutoLink comparisons in Figures 4(c) and A1. The earlier quantitative comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New Human3.6m controls remove the boundary loss, replace it with a sigmoid, remove link regularization, and replace the hierarchy with one 512-vector memory bank. Table A1 adds efficiency profiling at zero and three refinement iterations. Existing benchmark resolutions, metrics, masking ranges, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A8 adds direct tests of boundary enforcement, link regularization, and the benefit of multiple memory banks. Figures 4(c), A1, and A2 add background-related AutoLink comparisons, occlusion comparisons, and a severe-occlusion failure case. The earlier prior-initialization studies, sensitivity curves, occlusion curves, and masked-reference experiment are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v3 newly states that results are averaged over three experiment runs in Section 3.4 and Appendix A1; v2 supplies no run count. This establishes additional reporting, not an increase from a known earlier count. Neither version reports seed identities, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and appendix curves are unchanged, including the relocated PPL* results. New results include BKind's 2.44 on Human3.6m and Hedlin comparisons showing PPL ahead on Human3.6m and CUB-Aligned but behind on Taichi and every non-aligned CUB subset. New ablations report instability without the boundary loss, 2.70 with sigmoid replacement, and 2.64 without link regularization versus 2.56 for PPL. The single-bank result is internally inconsistent: Table A3 gives 2.62, while its discussion gives 2.72. Compute measurements and qualitative successes and failures are also added.

T1.justification: The prior definition, affine transformations, link aggregation, memory operations, and loss formulas are mathematically retained. Displayed equations are largely converted to inline notation. The added memory and rigidity discussion is conceptual explanation and qualification; no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, three enumerated contributions, and concluding claims about learned categorical priors and occlusion refinement remain essentially unchanged. The introduction adds comparative claims about learning without object masks and providing a lightweight, semantic, invariant representation through sparse keypoints rather than dense reconstruction.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of hierarchical retrieval and iterative correction, characterizes link-length regularization as an approximate 2D constraint on 3D rigidity, and explains the stabilizing roles of auxiliary losses. It explicitly warns that severe occlusion can produce plausible but incorrect reconstructions and compound errors. It also removes v2's assertion that compositional memory reduces data bias and discusses mixed outcomes against Hedlin. The existing limitation concerning 2D priors and rotations remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds the RTX A6000 hardware specification and training-time, inference-throughput, and GPU-memory measurements. It discloses 30-fps sampling and manual selection for the existing dog dataset, clarifies that Taichi's 5,000 frames train a linear regression, and explains the already evaluated CUB protocols. These are documentation additions, without evidence that the retained experiments changed. The promised future code, model, and data release remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against Wu et al. (2023), Li et al. (2024), and Hedlin et al. (2024), plus citations for two excluded datasets. It removes the compositional-memory related-work paragraph and its Deng and Seong citations while retaining the PCT comparison in the method. The two Sommer 2024 entries identify the same work already cited in v2.

P1.justification: The appendices are extensively reorganized: training techniques move before datasets, qualitative material is regrouped, and ablations are consolidated in A8. Section 3.3 is rewritten into labeled encoding, retrieval, and distillation stages, while inference explanations expand. The compositional-memory related-work subsection and standalone Impact Statement are removed. Much of the abstract, introduction, and conclusion remains verbatim.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 Tables 1–3 are consolidated into v3 Table 1, while PPL* results move to Table A4; new compute, diffusion-comparison, and ablation tables are added. Figure 4 gains a comparison panel, two qualitative appendix figures are added, and retained figures are resized and relocated. Numbered equations become inline, and v3 introduces overlapping heading and body text at Section 3.4.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the new loss and memory controls, stronger baseline comparisons, explicit occlusion failure case, and compute and repetition disclosures make the evidence more informative and easier to scrutinize. These gains are limited by the contradictory single-bank score in Table A3 versus its discussion and the lack of dispersion estimates for small ablation differences. The unchanged core method and benchmark results therefore receive useful but incomplete additional support.
